title: Slyde
tagline: An AI presentation studio I conceived, designed and launched — my vision, brought to life with AI.

body: Every agency rebuilds the same presentations from scratch, and every AI slide tool makes them look generic. I wanted a tool that writes like your company — one that learns from your best decks, case studies and brand voice, then builds new presentations in your own templates.

The bigger challenge was scope. Slyde isn't a prototype: it's a complete product — accounts, billing, real-time collaboration, a design-grade editor — plus a brand and a launch. I wanted to prove that one creative director, working AI-native, could take an idea that big from a sketch to a live product.

feature.caption: The Slyde launch film, made with AI in Blender and After Effects.

body: I started with the idea, not the interface: a company Brain. Slyde turns a team's past decks, case studies, website and voice into an organized knowledge base, then writes on-brand presentations from it — a brief or RFP goes in, a finished deck comes out. That idea shaped the positioning and the line that leads the brand: "Stop being generic. Use your brain."

I ran the build the way I'd run any production. I set the vision, wrote the briefs, made the product and design calls, and reviewed every feature until it felt right, with AI as the tools that turned that direction into working software. More than 2,800 commits later, Slyde has a Keynote-grade editor with smart guides and charts, real-time multiplayer with live cursors, chat and comments, an AI pipeline that drafts whole decks from a brief, PowerPoint and PDF import, editable PowerPoint export, and team workspaces with roles and paid plans.

The brand was mine end to end: the name (DeckForge, then Slydra, then Slyde), three design systems that landed on Product Pop's violet and paper, the messaging and the marketing site. I directed the launch film like any shoot — concept, script, look and edit — using AI to drive Blender and After Effects, and took it through 146 versions until every frame landed.
